name: Becfhola

attributes.attribute: protagonist of the Wooing of Becfhola
had an affair with the fairy lover Flann
represented Sovereignty as queen of Tara

sources: Cross, Tom Peete, and Clark Harris Slover, eds. Ancient Irish Tales. (New York: Henry Holt and Co., 1936), 533.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Becfhola is an Irish goddess or heroine. Her other names are Becfola and Beagfhola. She is a mortal queen of Tara. She is the central figure of the tale Tochmarc Becfhola, the Wooing of Becfhola. The tale tells of her affair with a fairy lover named Flann ua Fedach. As queen of Tara, Becfhola stands for the idea of Sovereignty. Her unhappiness with King Diarmait and her preference for the hero Crimthann may have cost Diarmait his right to rule. Becfhola planned a meeting with Crimthann on an island in Lough Erne. She met Flann instead and spent an enchanted night with him. She lived in fairy time while she was away. When she returned to Tara, no time appeared to have passed. Flann soon came to take her away.

okr.objective: Becfhola is a mortal queen of Tara whose fairy-time affair reshapes her place in Irish sovereignty myth.
